chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ṣāliḥ ibn al-Sindī, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Sometimes I perform wudu (ablution), and the water runs out, so I call the servant-girl, but she is slow in bringing me the water, and my wudu (ablution) dries. He said: “Repeat.”
So if an inquirer asks about the report which he narrated:

key_terms.الْجَارِيَةَ: the servant-girl who was called to bring water

ai.seo_question: If my wudu dries before I finish because the water was delayed, do I need to repeat it?
ai.summary: This report addresses a ruling related to wudu (ablution), specifically when continuity is interrupted and the previously washed parts dry before completion. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that the wudu (ablution) be repeated, indicating the legal significance of maintaining proper sequence and continuity in ritual purity.
